newsitem.title: UK: london gold uneasily steady, awaits next move.
newsitem.headline: london gold uneasily steady, awaits next move.

text.p: Gold prices were little changed from earlier levels on Monday afternoon as the market received mild help from the U.S. dollar.
"The dollar may be helping. It is certainly being watched, but nothing has really changed," a dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $340.40 per ounce compared with $341.00 this morning and Friday's lowest fix since April April 20, 1993 of $339.75.
At the fixing the Comex April contract was down $1.40 within forecast at $342.60 in thin volume.
Some dealers thought gold might be able to sustain an advance to $343-$344 although one added. "It has failed there in the past and I would not bet on it succeeding this time."
The dollar was firmer as dealers bought back positions sold before Saturday's Group of Seven (G7) economic summit in Berlin.
A communique after the meeting noted that "misalignments" in the currency markets had been corrected and that the group favoured stability in the markets.

Gold remained heavily oversold and while there was little reason to look for a recovery from $340.00, "...there is certainly good excuse for support in this region to hold," according to technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge.
However a dealer commented, "There is too much emotion about to be able to point to a particular number on the charts (to specify a floor)."
Silver held around $4.92/$4.94 -- down a cent -- all day having gained 16 cents by Friday's intraday high.
"Silver could be about to re-establish itself," one dealer said, noting that the gold-silver ratio was tightening as silver defied the weakness in gold.
The ratio stood at 68.39 on Monday down from 70.57 a week ago and 76.84 at the beginning of the year.
Platinum was $3.00 firmer at $352.00/$353.00 benefitting from firmness in sister metal palladium and increased plays on the widening gold-platinum spread.
"Playing the spread affects platinum much more than gold simply because it is a thinner market and buying platinum shows up in the price," a dealer said.
Palladium fixed at its highest level since July 23, 1996 of $134.25 on Monday afternoon reflecting gathering market tightness due to Russia not settling yet its 1997 supply contract to Japan.
